# The Name {#sec-the-name}

| For a month, give or take, it was called check.py:
| It was what the thing did, and the one who said it was I.

| Then came notes-check: more accurate, no better a name.
| Then a folder with four files inside. And the same
| Had befallen my notes: shoebox, spreadsheet, script, each outgrown;
| But this was the first one to need a name of its own.

| It needed one, since it was about to be a repo: at night
| I made changes I couldn't undo in the morning light.
| You can call a directory anything. Not anymore:
| You can't call a repository "the thing for chapter four".

| So I set aside an evening for names. I began
| In a document; by midnight, a page long, it ran.
| Most were puns. Punctuation rewards them, and shouldn't. One drew
| On the word *colon*; that one I hadn't thought through.

| None of them was a name: they were jokes, which I'd have to explain
| Every time that I typed one. I kept going, again and again,
| Which is how two in the morning happens. And then, around two,
| I gave up the page for a chat, with something else for Otto to do.

| I typed "quirk", and then Otto completed it: "quirework". I stayed
| With the word for a while. Not a pun: it sounded already made.
| But as far as I could find, it didn't exist. I checked.
| I liked it better than all of the page, or than what I'd select,

| And I'd spent the whole evening selecting. I don't recall, though,
| What I'd meant to ask Otto. That night, before I could say no,
| I made the repository. The first commit message was *Name it*.
| I've written better commit messages since. Not many, I'll admit.

| In the morning, a README: without one, repos look forsaken;
| And a version: without one, a tool looks a script. Zero point one was taken,
| Which promises nothing. The README ran a page, and no more:
| The shortest it ever would be. And chapter four
| Hadn't changed in weeks. It had never been that consistent before.

| That week it was no longer a script: name, repo, README, version. That was it:
| A tool. I was the only person who had ever used it.
